title: SAFE-MedPath: Patient-Disjoint Breast Histopathology Classification with Calibration Transfer Analysis and Conformal Uncertainty Quantification
content: Histopathology classifiers can be undermined by staining variability, patient-level data leakage, domain shift across tasks, and poorly calibrated probability outputs. We propose SAFE-MedPath, combining stain-oriented stochastic augmentation, a three-member ResNet-18 ensemble, post-hoc temperature scaling, and split-conformal prediction. BreaKHis is used for strictly patient-disjoint development, calibration, and testing; PatchCamelyon (PCam), whose endpoint (metastatic-tissue detection) differs from BreaKHis’s benign-versus-malignant task, is evaluated separately as an independent benchmark of architecture and training-recipe portability rather than same-task validation. Comparators are HOG+linear-SVM, HOG+RBF-SVM, and a single ResNet-18, all under an identical patient-disjoint protocol. On the BreaKHis test set, SAFE-MedPath achieved balanced accuracy 0.877 (95% CI 0.802–0.947), ROC-AUC 0.959, expected calibration error (ECE) 0.126, and split-conformal coverage 0.976 against a 0.90 target (mean prediction-set size 1.25). Ablation showed ensembling gave a small discrimination gain (+0.4 balanced-accuracy points) while stain augmentation and temperature scaling both hurt their target metric, indicating a validation-to-test calibration-transfer gap. On the independent PCam benchmark, the same architecture and recipe achieved balanced accuracy 0.821 and ROC-AUC 0.932. The full pipeline did not significantly improve discrimination over a single ResNet-18 (0.877 vs. 0.930; p=0.168 after Holm–Bonferroni correction), but converted that ensemble into a calibrated, uncertainty-aware output with 97.6% empirical coverage against a 90% target. The modest ensembling effect and calibration-transfer gap warrant further study before any clinical-use claim.
